reply.emotion: attentive and present, noticing something in the immediate environment
notes: Sentir has two main meanings: detecting a scent with your nose, or experiencing a physical or emotional feeling. Context usually makes it clear which one is intended.
If you want to say something has a pleasant smell, you can use 'sentir bon'. If it smells bad, use 'sentir mauvais'.

senses.definition: To notice or perceive an odor with your nose.

examples.text: Je sens une bonne odeur de cuisine.
examples.translation: I smell a good kitchen scent.
examples.emotion: hungry and expectant, delighted by the aroma

senses.definition: To have a physical sensation or to experience an emotion.

examples.text: Je me sens très fatigué aujourd'hui.
examples.emotion: lethargic and honest, admitting to exhaustion
examples.note: When used as a reflexive verb ('se sentir'), it almost always relates to your internal physical or emotional state.

definitions: To notice or perceive an odor with your nose.
To have a physical sensation or to experience an emotion.
